companyIntro.name: Helix Data Labs
companyIntro.mission: Turn messy business data into decisions people can trust and models that survive production.
companyIntro.culture: Evidence over opinion. A result is not a result until someone else can reproduce it.

projectBackground.name: Customer Churn Platform
projectBackground.context: A churn model reports 98% accuracy, but the retention team cannot reproduce the gain. A new retention offer has also been A/B tested.

manager.name: Lars de Vries
manager.role: Lead Data Scientist, Helix Data Labs
manager.note: If a number looks too good, assume it's wrong until proven otherwise. I want you to explain what the model does and what it doesn't.

assignment.title: Validate the churn model and the offer experiment
assignment.brief: Detect leakage, compute precision, recall and F1, evaluate the A/B lift and write a plain-language summary.

documents.name: Model Evaluation Report
documents.note: 98% accuracy; the base churn rate is 2%.

tasks.title: Spotting Leakage
tasks.prompt: A model uses 'cancellation_date' as a feature to predict cancellation. This is:
options: Data leakage — the feature contains the outcome
tasks.reasoning: Leakage gives unrealistic performance because information from the future or the target is included.
tasks.tip: Ask: would this be available at prediction time?
tasks.mistake: Leaky features inflate scores and fail in production.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Accuracy Paradox
tasks.prompt: Churn is 2% of customers. A model predicts 'no churn' for everyone and scores 98% accuracy. What does this show?
options: Accuracy is misleading on imbalanced data; use precision, recall or F1
tasks.reasoning: With rare events, accuracy can be high while the model is useless.
tasks.tip: Choose metrics that match the business cost.
tasks.mistake: Reporting accuracy alone hides a useless model.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: F1 Score
tasks.prompt: Using TP 80, FP 20, FN 40, compute the F1 score (round to 3 decimals).
tasks.reasoning: F1 balances precision and recall, which matters when both false alarms and misses cost money.
tasks.mistake: Averaging precision and recall arithmetically gives 0.733, not F1.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Relative Lift
tasks.prompt: Control converted at 4.0% (400/10,000) and the variant at 4.6% (460/10,000). What is the relative lift?
tasks.reasoning: Relative lift is the change over the control rate; the absolute difference is 0.6 percentage points.
tasks.tip: Report absolute and relative effects with a confidence interval.
tasks.mistake: Quoting 0.6% as the lift mixes percentage points and percent.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: A/B Test Validity
tasks.prompt: Select checks required before trusting the A/B result.
options: Stop as soon as the variant looks better
tasks.reasoning: Validity needs randomisation, planned sample size and sanity checks; peeking and selection bias invalidate results.
tasks.mistake: Stopping early or filtering on the outcome inflates false positives.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Stakeholder Summary
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence summary for the retention team: what the model can do, what the offer test shows and what you recommend.
tasks.modelAnswer: The model's 98% accuracy is misleading because only 2% of customers churn; its F1 score is 0.73, so it finds most churners but with some false alarms. A leaked cancellation feature inflated earlier numbers and has been removed. The retention offer lifted conversion from 4.0% to 4.6%, a 15% relative improvement, though we should confirm the confidence interval before rollout. I recommend launching the offer to a larger randomised group and using the model to prioritise customers, with monthly monitoring for drift.
tasks.reasoning: A good summary translates metrics into decisions and states uncertainty.
tasks.mistake: Technical jargon without a recommendation is not useful to stakeholders.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Model That Only Worked in the Notebook
caseStudy.background: A model scored 0.95 AUC in testing but failed in production. A feature had been computed using data available only after the customer had left.
caseStudy.challenges: The feature pipeline used future data during training.
questions: What validation would have exposed it?
How can feature availability be checked?
caseStudy.solution: Helix introduced time-based validation and a feature availability review before any model sign-off.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: If it wouldn't exist at prediction time, it can't be a feature.

options: The model sees information it won't have at prediction time
Harmonic mean of precision and recall
